policy.holds: an evaluator hold, an empty long or short side, or any member without a gap-free closed prefix ending at the deadline omits that deadline's weights, so the adapter holds the whole set for it
policy.rule: the registered #1787 basket evaluator called by the study on the same closed-bar input the runner gives the candidate: for every member, the last lookback_bars (60) closed daily bars ending with the bar that closes at the deadline, the frozen allocation context of this basket, and the training-selected return lookback, volatility lookback and quantile of the candidate; its exact weights become frozen baseline weights for that deadline.
policy.zero_signal: a member the evaluator gives weight 0 has target 0

policy.frequency_note: only an entry signal on the deadline bar itself counts; an entry signal on any other daily bar of the week leaves the member flat at that deadline, so this arm can be flat at most or all deadlines; the study reports how many deadlines carry a nonzero target
policy.holds: a member with fewer than 200 gap-free closed bars ending at the deadline, a non-finite z_score, adx or rsi on the deadline bar, or a signal other than -1, 0 or 1 omits that deadline's weights, so the adapter holds the whole set for it
policy.rule: the registered single-member evaluator with its frozen registered parameters, run separately for every eligible member on the last 200 closed daily bars ending with the bar that closes at the deadline; only the entry signal of that last bar is read: target weight = signal / N for N eligible members (+1 long entry, -1 short entry). The signal is never read as a position: Python keeps no state between deadlines, a zero signal sets a zero target, and unused allocation is never renormalized.
policy.zero_signal: signal 0 sets target 0, so the member is flat at that deadline
